summary: This program defines a small reusable block of code called a method and calls it twice from main. It shows how naming a task once lets you repeat it without retyping the work.

lines.text: Every Java program lives inside a class. The name must match the file name, so this code belongs in IntroFunction.java.
main is where Java starts running the program. Anything you want to happen has to be reachable from here.
This calls the method defined below. Control jumps down to that method, runs its body, then comes back to this spot.
The same call again, proving the point of methods: one definition, as many uses as you like.
The method definition. void means it hands nothing back to the caller, and the empty parentheses mean it needs no information to do its job.
The body of the method  or a total of two lines of output.
